who: Factory B builders, reviewers, CI jobs, and receiving implementation agents
what: A deterministic verifier for package manifest, hash, file-count, path, regular-file, and readable-member integrity
why: Every reusable Factory package needs a cheap independent byte/path integrity check before semantic verification or release review
when: After package creation, after transport/read-back, and before higher-level evidence or release decisions
where: Local Linux, GitHub Actions, or another environment with Python 3.11+
how: Read MANIFEST.json, validate required scalar types and declared rows, reject malformed/non-object rows, reject control-character/colon-bearing/non-canonical/dot/repeated-slash/Windows-drive paths, reject symlink directory roots and path components, validate ZIP directory entries before ignoring structural directories, enumerate directory contents fail-closed on scan errors, compare bytes/sizes/paths, optionally bind the manifest to an externally frozen SHA-256 trust anchor, and emit a machine-readable JSON receipt.
inputs: Factory package directory or ZIP containing MANIFEST.json; ZIP may use exactly one safe wrapper root
constraints: No extraction of ZIP content is required
approval_boundary: The verifier may report byte/path/readability integrity only; external release still requires the governing Release Contract and scoped approval
failure_modes: Unreadable directory enumeration that could hide unexpected members
Unsafe ZIP directory entries including symlink/traversal/absolute directory metadata
Control-character, colon-bearing, dot-segment, repeated-slash, Windows-drive, traversal, or absolute paths
Malformed required manifest scalar types (schema_version, candidate, file_count, size)
Malformed or missing manifest, including non-object files[] rows
Symlink subject root, symlink path component, leaf symlink, resolved target outside the package root, or non-regular file
Corrupt or otherwise unreadable directory/ZIP member
recovery: Rebuild the package from the frozen source candidate and regenerate the manifest
Treat malformed/unreadable/corrupt members as FAIL evidence rather than allowing an exception to escape
success_criteria: Corrupt ZIP member returns a machine-readable FAIL receipt
Malformed non-object MANIFEST files[] row returns FAIL without an uncaught exception
Directory parent-symlink and subject-root-symlink negative controls fail with zero verified files
Anchored mode rejects coordinated payload+manifest substitution against the frozen manifest hash
Malformed required scalar types fail closed instead of passing via Python bool/int equality or mere key presence
NUL/non-canonical manifest paths fail closed without uncaught path exceptions
Unsafe ZIP directory entries fail closed while normal explicit directory entries remain supported
Unreadable directory enumeration emits FAIL evidence instead of silently hiding unexpected members
Control-character and colon-bearing/Windows ADS-like paths fail closed before member lookup
known_limitations: Without an external expected MANIFEST.json SHA-256, PASS proves self-consistency only and cannot detect coordinated payload+manifest substitution
v1 supports the current Factory B MANIFEST.json shape
ZIP wrapper support is limited to exactly one safe top-level wrapper directory
Concurrent filesystem mutation between path validation and byte read is not claimed to be hardened
It proves byte/path/readability consistency, not semantic quality, provenance truth, or release approval
